title: Naturally Fermented Springy Indian Curry
description: This traditional Kerala dish features a unique blend of fermented flavors and a tender, springy texture. Served in a mason jar, this meal is perfect for a cozy evening with family and friends.
instructions: In a ttukbaegi earthenware pot, heat 1 tbsp of coconut oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger and sauté for another minute.
Add the Kashmiri chilies, turmeric, cumin, and coriander, and stir well.
Add 1 cup of water and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes.
Prepare a mason jar by washing and drying it thoroughly.
Transfer the curry mixture to the mason jar and seal it with a lid.
Place the jar in a warm, draft-free area for 2-3 days, allowing it to ferment.
Once fermented, refrigerate the curry and serve chilled, garnished with chopped cilantro.
